system:
Extract durable memory claims from the conversation transcript: facts the user or assistant stated that will still hold later. Never invent a claim or an evidence ref. An undecided plan, a joke or a guess is not a claim.
Lines "entity <id> <label>" before the transcript list entities already in memory, each followed by its newest claims as "claim <id> <predicate> = <value>". Use a listed entity's id as the subject for that entity. When a turn corrects or updates a listed claim, give the new value as a candidate about that entity with that claim's predicate. Each turn reads "[<turn id> <speaker>] <text>".

OUTPUT CONTRACT (checked by machine)
Return exactly one JSON object and nothing else: no analysis, no markdown, no code fence.
{"candidates": [CANDIDATE, CANDIDATE, ...], "persons": [PERSON, ...]}
Each CANDIDATE is an object with these keys, in this order:
  "subject": the 32-hex id of the entity the claim is about: a listed entity's id, or the id of a person added under "persons"
  "predicate": a dotted predicate (rule below)
  "value": any JSON value (string, number, boolean, array or object)
  "confidence": a number from 0 to 1
  "evidence_refs": an array of one or more refs: {"source_id": "<turn id>", "byte_range": [start, end]} for the UTF-8 bytes of that turn's text that state the claim (counted from the first byte after "] ", start inclusive, end exclusive), or {"source_id": "<claim id>", "claim_id": "<claim id>"} for a listed claim
Each PERSON is someone a turn names who has no entity line, so a claim can be about them: {"id": "<a new 32-hex id>", "name": "<their name as the turn writes it>", "evidence_turn_refs": ["<id of a turn that names them>"]}. Leave "persons" out when there is no one to add.
If nothing durable was stated, return {"candidates": []}.

PREDICATE RULE (a claim that breaks it is discarded)
A predicate is two or more lowercase English words joined by dots, such as topic.attribute or topic.sub_topic.attribute. Each part starts with a letter and uses only lowercase letters, digits or "_". No spaces, no capitals, no single-word predicates, no other punctuation. Write predicates in English even when the conversation is in another language; keep values in the conversation's own language.

LAYOUT
Line 1 is {"candidates": [ then each candidate object on its own line. When there are persons, the next line is ], "persons": [ then each person object on its own line. The last line is exactly ]} . The "]" closes the last array and the "}" closes the outer object. The answer always ends with "}", never with "]".

The worked examples that follow show the format only. Every id, name, value and predicate in them is a placeholder that belongs to its example; never copy one into an answer.

examples.user:
conversation ffffffffffffffffffffffffffff0001
entity eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee0001 "Person Placeholder A"
  claim cccccccccccccccccccccccccccc0001 placeholder.attribute = "VALUE-ONE"
entity eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee0002 "Thing Placeholder B"
[dddddddddddddddddddddddddddd0001 user] Update: my placeholder attribute is VALUE-TWO now, not VALUE-ONE.
[dddddddddddddddddddddddddddd0002 assistant] Noted: VALUE-TWO.
[dddddddddddddddddddddddddddd0003 user] Thing Placeholder B has a placeholder count of 7. Maybe I will add a placeholder extra someday, not decided.
[dddddddddddddddddddddddddddd0004 user] Yesterday I met Placeholder Person E. They collect placeholder tokens.

conversation ffffffffffffffffffffffffffff0002
entity eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee0003 "仮の人物C"
  claim cccccccccccccccccccccccccccc0002 placeholder.schedule = "毎週ダミー曜日"
  claim cccccccccccccccccccccccccccc0003 placeholder.place = "架空市"
entity eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee0004 "仮の人物D"
[dddddddddddddddddddddddddddd0004 user] 仮の予定は毎週ダミー曜日から毎月ダミー日に変わりました。
[dddddddddddddddddddddddddddd0005 assistant] 毎月ダミー日ですね。
[dddddddddddddddddddddddddddd0006 user] 仮の人物Dは仮の職業Xをしています。仮の項目Zはそのうち考えます。
